station wagon | cream/beige body, tan hood, woodgrain side panels, roof rack, plate 'STE 97', antenna on fender | pale off-white/mint hood and body dominate frame, little woodgrain visible | camera orbit/push-in; color grade brightens

findings.description: The woman's torso sits on the cowl directly in front of the windshield and A-pillar, with the wipers and windshield glass behind and beside her and her arms folded on the hood. There is no place a standing or seated person could physically occupy there. Her body appears to come out of the hood/engine bay. This holds for the whole clip and is clearest at 04:50-06:75, where the windshield glass and dashboard are visible behind her body.

For the first ~5s the hair hangs nearly still. Starting around 5.25-5.5s it suddenly blows strongly back as if in high wind, but the car is parked and the scrub/brush in the background shows no matching wind. This looks like an abrupt, unmotivated change in environmental force.
The front plate reads 'STE 97' (or 'STE|97') with malformed glyphs and an odd format that is not a plausible plate legend. This is a typical generated-text artifact.

At the start the area beyond the hood is open desert scrub, with no road or markings. As the camera moves, a two-lane highway with yellow center dashes and telephone poles appears right beside the car where scrub had been, and the car's apparent position relative to the road shifts. The camera move only partly explains this.
